scope.summary: MembershipRolePolicy: Implement Owner, Manager, Editor, Commenter, and Viewer project or workspace MembershipRole as policy input with explicit grant-management actions and no blanket resource read.
scope.objective: Implement Owner, Manager, Editor, Commenter, and Viewer project or workspace MembershipRole as policy input with explicit grant-management actions and no blanket resource read.
expected_behavior: Implement Owner, Manager, Editor, Commenter, and Viewer project or workspace MembershipRole as policy input with explicit grant-management actions and no blanket resource read.
Preserve all pre-existing behavior and original WP intent not explicitly superseded by Master Spec v02.202.
Authorize at the executable backend before filtering or personalization; client and UI identifiers are selectors, never authority.
Emit account, Principal, session, AccessSpace, resource, delegation, correlation, action, result, and policy attribution for success, denial, failure, retry, and recovery paths.
scope.candidate_surface_rule: Candidate paths are grounded in current handshake_main topology but must be re-discovered and narrowed during refinement and packet activation; do not invent a parallel subsystem when an existing product seam owns the behavior.

implementation_steps: Read all no-context authority, confirm packet activation, and confirm dependency verdicts.
Inspect current implementation and write a failing targeted test or reproducible negative proof for the exact objective.
Lock exact schemas, APIs, migrations, event families, resources, and enforcement boundaries before implementation.
Implement the smallest complete behavior through existing product seams.
Wire PostgreSQL and EventLedger or Flight Recorder plus ResourceBroker, search, memory, model, tool, export, diagnostic, and UI boundaries that consume the changed resource.
Add success, wrong-account, wrong-Space, same-project-private, stale or revoked context, metadata side-channel, concurrency, restart, and derived-scope tests as applicable.
Update the in-product UserManual in the same change with purpose, route or command, inputs, outputs, failure, recovery, privacy, and diagnostic posture.
For GUI work, use native Handshake UI, stable AccessKit and Argus author IDs, headless steering, re-observation, screenshot or tree evidence, layout, accessibility, and renderer-error scans.
Run targeted and regression proof, inspect exact artifacts, record HBR evidence, and hand off through governed receipts.
acceptance_criteria: The product implements exactly this objective: Implement Owner, Manager, Editor, Commenter, and Viewer project or workspace MembershipRole as policy input with explicit grant-management actions and no blanket resource read.

Every touched primary and derived resource has stable owner, account, Principal, session, AccessSpace, ResourceGrant, lineage, and policy linkage, or the official refinement records a valid NOT_APPLICABLE reason.
Wrong-account, wrong-Space, same-project-private, stale or revoked, forged-selector, and metadata-side-channel cases fail closed where applicable.
Derived outputs, indexes, previews, caches, logs, contexts, exports, backups, and remote copies cannot widen source visibility.
EventLedger and Flight Recorder cover success, denial, failure, retry or recovery, actor versus owner, and delegation without leaking restricted metadata.
No SQLite, Docker, application-only, UI-only, or mock-only proof substitutes for real PostgreSQL and executable product boundaries.
The UserManual is current and a no-context model can operate and recover the behavior.

same_project_private_resource_cases: Two accounts are members of one project; only explicitly shared resources are mutually visible.
cross_account_negative_cases: forged account, Principal, session, Space, or resource IDs
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: preview, index, cache, log, context, export, or backup does not widen source scope

risk_if_missed: Omitting or compressing MembershipRolePolicy leaves this obligation unimplemented or encourages a second authorization model, causing cross-account leakage, weak Flight Recorder attribution, or future shared-workspace and SaaS rework.

risks: MembershipRolePolicy may pass a happy-path test while failing its exact objective under denied, failure, restart, or concurrent conditions.
Authorization may exist only in UI or application code while PostgreSQL, filesystem, search, model, tool, export, or diagnostic paths bypass it.
Failure, never-started, cache, index, diagnostic, export, or derived paths may omit scope and leak restricted existence.
Concurrent revocation or context switching may race with a previously authorized operation.
minimum_controls: Start with executable RED behavior against the exact current product seam.
Enforce at every real resource boundary and test table-owner, runtime-role, path, API, search, model, and tool bypass attempts that apply.
Use stable resource lineage and source-scope intersection for every derivative and projection.
Use policy and revocation versions, bounded leases, cancellation or explicit pinned-context behavior, and concurrent tests.
